title: head-wise-pad-and-layer-split-prefetch-for-mqa-qwen-performance-improvements
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: MQA/GQA execution on some Qwen and Llama model variants showed transient memory spikes and tail-latency regressions when handling heterogeneous head widths and long-context KV cache prefetch. This PR introduces two complementary runtime optimizations: 1) head-wise padding to coalesce multi-head matmuls into head-groups with uniform width so kernels can use contiguous memory and avoid per-head shuffles; 2) layer-split prefetch that overlaps KV shard transfer with upstream attention computation by splitting the attention pipeline into a prefetch/compute schedule. Secondary changes include a conservative backpressure tweak for continuous batching so we don't accept batches that will blow peak GPU memory when prefetch is in-flight, and a Qwen-specific rotary offset fast-path to avoid expensive fallback for a known rotary encoding layout. Key outcomes: on internal perf harness (qwen-7b-mqa long-context synthetic traces) median latency down 8-18% depending on seqlen and batch mix, 95th percentile tail latency down 12-24%, and end-to-end token-cost reduction ~6-12% due to better packing and fewer fallback kernels. Implementation notes: head-wise padding is opt-in per-model via model config hint (model_config.runtime.head_pad_grouping); layer-split prefetch has a tunable window (runtime.scheduling.layer_prefetch_window_ms) and defaults conservatively to 8ms. See ENG-3241 and benchmark job links for raw data. Checklist: [x] perf microbench added, [x] unit tests for pad grouping and ordering, [x] e2e regression against existing KV cache testcases, [x] docs note and config defaults, [x] added canary flag for rollout. Follow-ups: automated quantile-based tuning for prefetch window (ENG-3308), expanded kernels to support dynamic head groups for mixed-precision models. Related PRs: ties into adaptive-kernel-routing work and the scheduler heuristics changes in previous releases.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Nice approach — do we have any regressions on non-MQA models when head_pad_grouping is unset? Please add a guard so default is noop.
Maya Patel: Guard added; default path retains current behavior. Confirmed zero-regressions on Llama-2-13B baseline (unit+smoke).
Zoe Chen: The prefetch window looks promising but could overshoot GPU memory for small-instance Dedicated customers. Can we expose a per-pool override and document the safety knob?
Maya Patel: Added runtime.scheduling.layer_prefetch_window_ms per-pool override and documented in perf_tuning.md. Also added canary flag for staged rollout to Dedicated pools.
Ravi Mehta: I saw one flaky CI failure (tests/perf::mqa_long_context_bench) on first run due to timing on CI VMs. Re-ran -> passed. Please add a tolerant assertion and a retry in test harness.
Maya Patel: Added retry and relaxed clock guards; pushed fix. All CI checks now green.
Zoe Chen: Approved after minor docs nit. Liam approved. Ravi approved.
release_notes: Runtime: Add optional head-wise padding and layer-split prefetch to reduce latency and memory spikes for MQA/GQA workloads. Conservative defaults; opt-in per-model and per-pool overrides available.
